text:
Dmitri Simashev, the sixth pick in 2023, had one point in 28 games last season. Through 20 games this year he has four goals and six points, and the jump looks earned. His ice time is up (16.5 minutes over his last ten, with two games past 21), and he is getting to better ice: 1.2 expected goals on his own shots over that stretch against 0.8 usual.

Is the finishing real? Partly. Four goals on 2.12 expected is a hot hand, and a 20% shooting rate from a defenseman won't last. But the process behind it is genuine. NHL EDGE has him with 23 skating bursts over 20 mph (94th percentile), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in a small sample last season, had 44% of his shots coming off the rush. The Athletic's Jesse Granger described his goal against Vegas: "He beats Hart with a wrist shot from the high slot."

The worry is defensive. Utah has been 12 points worse by shot quality with him on the ice than without. Defensemen drafted around him usually score about 0.30 points a game in their first full year, which is exactly his pace.
headline: Dmitri Simashev's goals are not a fluke
